causal_chain: A learned exclusion gate can downweight states contradicted by the current positive-vs-negative comparison, reducing false attraction from mixed histories.
A small bank of persistent user states can preserve distinct taste modes that would otherwise be averaged away in single-embedding collaborative filters.
Better separation on hard pairwise comparisons should transfer to improved offline full-sort NDCG@10.
Candidate scores formed from routed state-to-item compatibility should therefore separate true positives from confusing substitutes more effectively than static single-state scoring.
Event-conditioned transport over the user's train-only interaction history can update state relevance toward the current positive item without requiring held-out access or online signals.
Users in ML-1M often mix multiple stable tastes rather than expressing one globally consistent preference vector.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count or regularization effects rather than from state transport and exclusion routing; a matched-capacity single-state scorer or ungated multi-state average could account for improvements if the proposed mechanism is not the real cause.
discriminative_predictions: Removing event-conditioned transport while keeping multiple persistent states should reduce gains more than removing a small amount of regularization, indicating that dynamic routing rather than raw capacity matters.
The exclusion gate should most help on negatives that are close to one user state but inconsistent with the routed state mixture implied by the positive item.
The full mechanism should outperform a mechanism-off single-state control at similar embedding budget on full-sort NDCG@10.
Users with more diverse training histories should show larger relative improvement than users with very concentrated histories.
expected_evidence: A measurable gap between the proposed model and a matched single-state mechanism-off under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Ablations showing degradation when either state transport or exclusion gating is removed.
Per-user or per-history-diversity stratification indicating larger benefits for mixed-interest users.
Training logs confirming the candidate remains stable and executable within the qualification budget.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched-capacity single-state or ungated multi-state control matches or exceeds the proposed model on full-sort NDCG@10, or if removing transport/exclusion leaves performance unchanged, the central mechanism claim is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core representation from one user vector to a persistent state bank, changes the interaction structure by routing each pairwise comparison through event-conditioned memory transport, and changes the scoring relation by introducing an explicit exclusion gate that suppresses contradictory state evidence. These are architectural and relational changes, not a parameter retune or light wrapper over an existing profile operator.
research_spec.hypothesis: A candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small bank of persistent latent preference states, transports state relevance through the user's train-only interaction history conditioned on the current positive item, and applies a learned exclusion gate against the sampled negative item will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filters because it preserves multi-intent preference structure while explicitly suppressing contradictory evidence during pairwise ranking.
implementation_requirements: Build train-only user histories from the frozen training interactions, optionally ordered by training timestamp when available, with no held-out access.
Compute an exclusion gate from the contrast between positive- and negative-conditioned routed evidence, and use it to subtract contradictory state contributions before final scoring.
Compute positive-conditioned routing weights over the K states using compatibility between transported states and the positive item embedding.
For each training triple (u, i+, i-), compute history-conditioned attention from each user state to historical item embeddings and derive transported state summaries.
Implement a new RecBole GeneralRecommender with user_state_bank [n_users, K, d] and item embeddings [n_items, d].
Implement full-sort prediction by reusing the routed user representation and scoring against all item embeddings without accessing validation/test interactions.
Include executable ablations for mechanism-off and for transport/gate removal within the same candidate code path.
Train with a pairwise BPR-style loss on s(u,i+) - s(u,i-) plus standard regularization terms.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched-capacity mechanism-off control that keeps comparable embedding dimensionality and parameter budget but collapses the user state bank to a single static user embedding and removes both event-conditioned transport and exclusion gating.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Replace static single-vector user scoring with a multi-state memory architecture: persistent user states are softly transported over train-only historical items, routed by the current positive item, and filtered by a subtractive exclusion gate before scoring candidate items.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Executable mechanism-off: same candidate-local GeneralRecommender skeleton, optimizer, loss, and approximate parameter budget, but set K=1 effectively, remove history transport, remove exclusion gating, and score items with a standard static user-item dot product using only the collapsed user embedding and item embedding.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: A 3-state user memory model with one transport step over each user's train-only history and one exclusion gate in pairwise scoring, compared against the matched mechanism-off single-state collapse under the frozen ML-1M full-sort protocol.
research_spec.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does a train-only multi-state user memory with event-conditioned transport and exclusion gating improve NDCG@10 over a matched single-state collaborative filtering control?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: A compact implementation with small K (for example 3-4 states) and one transport step should fit within the qualification budget because scoring remains embedding-based and the additional cost is limited to short train-only history aggregation and lightweight gating per pairwise batch.

causal_chain: A small bank of persistent user states can store separable preference modes without requiring session labels.
Conditioning a transport operator on the user's recent training-history items lets the model shift state emphasis toward the intent most relevant to the current scoring context.
Pairwise training then reinforces both which state should win for a positive item and how recent evidence should transport the state mixture away from negatives.
This should improve full-sort ranking when held-out positives align with one latent taste mode that would be diluted in single-embedding collaborative filters.
Users in ML-1M often express mixed tastes that are poorly summarized by one static user vector.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from increased parameter count or an extra nonlinear scorer rather than from multi-state memory transport itself.
discriminative_predictions: Ablating transport while keeping the same state bank should reduce performance more on users whose recent training interactions differ from their long-run average profile, indicating the benefit is not only static multi-intent capacity.

Compared with a matched single-state mechanism-off control, the proposed model should show larger improvements for users with longer and more genre-diverse training histories than for short, homogeneous histories.
The learned routing weights over user states should be sharper for positives than sampled negatives, whereas the mechanism-off control has no such state-selective separation.
expected_evidence: Internal diagnostics show non-collapsed usage of multiple states and nontrivial transport updates from recent-history context.
Qualification runs produce a measurable NDCG@10 delta versus the matched mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
User-slice analysis by history diversity or recency-shift shows concentrated gains in mixed-taste users.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched single-state or no-transport control matches or exceeds the candidate on full-sort NDCG@10, or if the candidate collapses to effectively uniform state usage across users and items, the memory-transport mechanism is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core representation from one user embedding to a user-specific state set, changes the interaction structure by routing scores through state selection conditioned on candidate and recent history, and adds a custom transport capability that updates the scoring state from ordered training interactions. These are mechanism-level changes rather than tuning or shallow wrappers.
research_spec.hypothesis: A candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small bank of persistent latent preference states and scores each item through recent-history-conditioned transport plus disagreement-aware state routing will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-state collaborative filtering, because it can preserve multiple long-run tastes while shifting toward the intent most supported by the user's recent training interactions.
implementation_requirements: Build per-user ordered training histories from the frozen train split timestamps only; do not access validation or test interactions for state updates.
Compute candidate-item score by routing over transported user states with candidate-conditioned attention or softmax gating.
Generate a transport delta from recent-history context to update each user state before scoring.
Implement a candidate-local GeneralRecommender with pairwise BPR-style loss and full-sort prediction over all items.
Log diagnostics for state usage entropy, transport magnitude, and slice metrics by user history diversity.
Maintain K learnable user state embeddings plus item embeddings and a recent-history context encoder based on the last L training items.
Provide an executable mechanism-off variant in the same codebase that removes transport and state routing while preserving pairwise training and comparable parameter budget.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use a candidate-local matched control with the same optimizer, item embeddings, training loop, pairwise loss family, and approximately matched parameter count, but with a single user state and no recent-history-conditioned transport or candidate-conditioned state routing.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a Multi-State Transported Preference Routing recommender: each user owns K persistent latent states; recent training-history items are encoded into a context vector; this context produces a transport update applied to the state bank; for each candidate item, a routing gate selects or mixes transported states based on state-item compatibility and state-context disagreement; the final score is the gated affinity between the candidate item and transported user states.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is a matched single-state affinity model implemented in the same candidate-local class family: replace the user state bank with one user embedding, disable recent-history-conditioned transport, disable candidate-conditioned routing, and score by a direct user-item dot product under the same pairwise training and full-sort evaluation protocol.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: A two-condition qualification: (1) the proposed multi-state transported routing model and (2) a matched mechanism-off single-state no-transport control, both trained once under the frozen ML-1M protocol with identical data pipeline and comparable parameter budget.
research_spec.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does adding recent-history-conditioned transport over a small bank of persistent user preference states improve ranking beyond a matched single-state collaborative filter?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The candidate is feasible within the stated budget because ML-1M is small enough to cache ordered user histories in memory, the transport module can be implemented with lightweight MLP projections over recent-item averages, and full-sort scoring remains standard matrix multiplication plus a small routing step per user batch.

causal_chain: A candidate-local recommender that augments direct user-item affinity with a short-history intent encoder and a separately learned user residual memory introduces a new executable capability: persistent correction signals that are conditionally activated only when recent history indicates the relevant intent.

Because the proposal includes an explicit mechanism-off realization that preserves most components while disabling the residual contribution, any gain can be attributed more sharply to the residual-memory mechanism rather than incidental implementation changes.

If repeated ranking errors are caused by missing reusable correction state rather than only better negatives or regularization, the gated residual pathway should improve hard-positive recovery over a matched direct-affinity control.
The accepted context identifies a real gap: earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and an executable mechanism-off, so prior high-change ideas were hard to falsify cleanly.

The current executable family is dominated by static user/item embeddings or graph propagation variants, which do not provide an explicit reusable correction state for repeated pairwise mistakes concentrated in mixed-interest users.
research_spec.closest_parent: The current profile is mechanistically weak because its user representation is fit as a largely static preference vector, so repeated pairwise mistakes on niche or temporally local interests do not become an explicit reusable correction signal. A descendant that maintains a learned user-level residual memory and gates it against a short-history intent encoder will better recover hard positives and improve full-sort ranking.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any observed improvement could come from merely adding capacity through extra parameters and a recent-history encoder, not from persistent user residual memory. Under that explanation, a matched model with the same short-history encoder and similar parameter count but with residual-memory contribution disabled should perform similarly.
discriminative_predictions: If gains come only from recent-history encoding, then disabling the residual-memory contribution while keeping the short-history encoder should largely preserve performance.

If persistent correction memory is the operative mechanism, the full model should outperform its mechanism-off control most strongly for users with diverse or conflicting training histories, where static representations are likeliest to blur intent.
If the hypothesis is wrong, the mechanism-off control and the full model should have similar full-sort NDCG@10 despite the added residual pathway.
expected_evidence: A measurable separation between the full model and its mechanism-off control on validation/test full-sort NDCG@10 under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Ablation showing that zeroing residual memory at scoring time erodes any advantage that is present in the full model.
Larger relative gains on user subsets with higher historical item diversity or shorter-term preference shifts measured from train interactions only.
research_spec.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if the matched mechanism-off control performs indistinguishably from or better than the full model on full-sort NDCG@10 under the frozen protocol, especially if no stronger effect appears on mixed-interest users.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal requires a candidate-local recommender with a dual-state user representation: a persistent residual memory plus a short-history intent encoder, combined through a learned gate at scoring time. That introduces custom state construction and user-conditional fusion not available as a parameterized variant of the current executable profile's static MF or LightGCN operator families.
research_spec.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that combines direct user-item affinity with a gated user residual memory conditioned on a short recent-history intent encoder will rank held-out items better than a matched direct-affinity control, because repeated pairwise errors on niche or local interests become a persistent reusable correction signal instead of being absorbed into a single static user representation.
implementation_requirements: Build train-only per-user chronological interaction histories from the frozen training split.
Encode a fixed-length recent-history summary from item embeddings using a lightweight order-aware module such as gated averaging or a small GRU implemented in PyTorch.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender compatible with pairwise training and full-sort prediction.
Learn a separate user residual-memory embedding table and a gate that mixes direct user embedding, recent-history intent summary, and residual memory when scoring candidate items.
Provide an executable matched mechanism-off variant in the same codepath by forcing the residual-memory contribution to zero while retaining the same direct-affinity and recent-history components.
Support full-sort scoring for all items without accessing held-out interactions.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the identical architecture, optimizer family, training data, and recent-history encoder, but set the residual-memory contribution to zero at train and inference time so the only removed mechanism is persistent user residual correction.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-state user model: a base user embedding for stable affinity, a learned persistent residual-memory vector for correction, and a gate driven by recent interacted item embeddings that decides how much residual correction should influence each candidate score.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Executable mechanism-off: keep the same item embeddings, base user embeddings, recent-history intent encoder, pairwise loss, and full-sort scorer, but deterministically clamp the residual-memory gate to zero and omit the residual-memory term from the score. This yields a matched direct-affinity-plus-recent-intent control without persistent correction memory.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: Add only one new mechanism beyond a matched direct-affinity-plus-recent-intent control: a learned persistent user residual-memory vector whose contribution is activated by a recent-history-conditioned gate during pairwise training and full-sort inference.
research_spec.observed_failure_mode: Accepted context explicitly notes that earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off, preventing clean falsification of high-change mechanisms.
research_spec.research_question: Does adding an explicit persistent user residual-memory pathway, gated by short recent-history intent, improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over a matched control that has recent-history context but no residual correction memory?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The model should fit within the stated development budget on ML-1M because it uses only embedding tables, a lightweight recent-history encoder, simple gating layers, and standard pairwise training; the main extra cost versus MF is train-only history caching and modest additional per-batch sequence aggregation.

causal_chain: A candidate-conditioned retrieval module can separate historical items into supportive and opposing subsets instead of collapsing all history into one static user vector.
Learning distinct support and opposition aggregators creates a per-candidate comparison state that changes across the catalog during full-sort scoring.
Pairwise optimization teaches the model to increase positive scores when support dominates and decrease negative scores when opposition dominates.
This selective evidence decomposition should especially help ambiguous, substitute-heavy, and niche candidates where static collaborative filters over-trust aggregate co-occurrence.
Users with mixed-taste histories contain both evidence that supports a candidate and evidence that should suppress it.
research_spec.closest_parent: Explicitly learning a user-conditioned exclusion memory and subtractive gate alongside standard attraction embeddings will improve ranking quality because many hard negatives are not merely low-affinity items; they are items that align with patterns the user's history implicitly avoids.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from increased parameter count or generic attention over user history rather than from explicitly decomposing support versus opposition evidence.
discriminative_predictions: A mechanism-off ablation that keeps candidate-conditioned history attention but removes the opposition channel should lose most of the benefit on substitute-heavy items while retaining less change on head items.
Compared with a matched single-channel attentive history model, the proposed mechanism should show larger gains for users whose histories contain weakly coherent or multi-cluster neighborhoods.

If the support/opposition split is causal, score margins for hard negatives that are close to some historical items but conflict with the dominant user pattern should improve more than margins for easy negatives.
expected_evidence: Ablation evidence that removing the opposition pathway degrades ranking more than a similar-sized parameter reduction elsewhere.
Improved full-sort NDCG@10 versus the matched control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Per-user analysis showing larger relative gains for higher history-diversity users.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched single-channel candidate-conditioned history attention control matches or exceeds the proposed model, then explicit support-opposition decomposition is not the operative mechanism.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This candidate changes the core interaction structure from static user-item compatibility or graph propagation into candidate-conditioned decomposition over each user's historical set, with separate learned support and opposition evidence paths and subtractive scoring. That requires custom executable capability beyond the active profile catalog's existing BPR_MF and LIGHTGCN descendants and is not a parameter-only or wrapper modification.
research_spec.hypothesis: A recommender that scores each user-item pair by candidate-conditioned decomposition of the user's history into supportive and opposing evidence channels, then combines direct affinity with support-minus-opposition aggregation, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filters because it can promote candidates justified by a specific subset of history while actively discounting contradictory historical evidence.
implementation_requirements: Aggregate support and opposition history representations with masked attention over the user's observed training history.
For each candidate item, compute similarity between the candidate embedding and each historical item embedding, then route similarities through separate learned support and opposition kernels.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with user and item embeddings plus a padded user-history cache built from training interactions only.

Provide an executable mechanism-off variant that preserves the same embeddings and candidate-conditioned attention machinery but collapses support and opposition into a single non-signed history channel.
Score each user-item pair with a fusion of direct user-item affinity, support-context alignment, and subtractive opposition-context alignment.
Train with pairwise BPR-style loss using protocol-compliant negative sampling and support full-sort prediction over all items at evaluation time.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the same embedding sizes, optimizer family, training loop, history cache, and candidate-conditioned attention computation, but replace the signed dual-channel support/opposition decomposition with a single-channel attentive history aggregation and additive score fusion.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a candidate-conditioned dual-evidence retriever over each user's training history that produces separate support and opposition context vectors and uses their signed difference in scoring.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Disable signed decomposition by sharing one attention kernel for all historical evidence, remove the opposition context term from scoring, and replace support-minus-opposition with a single additive attentive history context while keeping the same embeddings, history inputs, and pairwise training recipe.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: A Dual-Evidence History Router model: user/item embeddings, per-user training-history cache, candidate-conditioned support attention, candidate-conditioned opposition attention, and a signed fusion scorer trained with pairwise ranking loss.
research_spec.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does candidate-conditioned separation of supportive versus opposing historical evidence improve ranking beyond a matched single-channel attentive collaborative recommender?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The model is feasible within the stated budget because ML-1M histories are short enough for padded masked attention over user histories during pairwise training and chunked full-sort scoring; the main cost is candidate-history interaction tensors, which can be controlled with vectorized batched computation and evaluation chunking.
